newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA SEES ARMS SPENDING DECISION BEFORE END-97.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA SEES ARMS SPENDING DECISION BEFORE END-97.

text.p: Deputy Defence Minister Ronnie Kasrils said on Thursday that cabinet discussion of arms spending could not be rushed but he hoped South Africa would decide its priorities before the end of the year.

South Africa's defence review, which has taken 16 months so far, was due to have gone before a cabinet meeting on Wednesday but the status of the meeting was downgraded because neither President Nelson Mandela nor Deputy President Thabo Mbeki attended.

Kasrils told state radio on Thursday the ministers who discussed the review on Wednesday had commented "very favourably" but because no cabinet ruling on the document could be made, it could not go before parliament for debate and final approval.

Kasrils and Defence Minister Joe Modise are pinning their hopes for the acquisition of four corvettes and a number of submarines on acceptance of the defence review, which lays out the country's arms needs for the foreseeable future.
Shipyards in Britain, Spain, Germany and France are keen to win any contracts emerging from the review.
"Cabinet needs to study the review, it's a 10-chapter book, and there are still a number of items that need to be developed later this year," Kasrils said.

"We're not in a hurry to have the review endorsed, although we would like to see it endorsed this year... We'll have to wait until we clear everything with cabinet because the document can't come before parliament until that happens," he said.
"The parliamentary standing committee on defence has endorsed the review, which cleared it to go through to cabinet. So the key aspect now...is at the door of cabinet...
"We accept and understand the question really is, how much can we reasonably afford for defence. That's why we can't rush cabinet into that decision," Kasrils said.
Modise has asked Mbeki to intervene in a dispute with Finance Minister Trevor Manuel over cuts in arms spending which Modise says are emasculating the defence force.
